title: Cluster init sequencing constraints and Terraform interface notes
content:
Purpose
This doc collects notes for a pragmatic cluster initialization sequencing model and a thin Terraform module interface to cover both bare-metal and vSphere on-prem installs. Aim is to reduce fragile implicit steps during field installs and make upgrades/rollbacks predictable. This is a working draft — contains hypotheses, test steps, and suggested module variables for discussion.

Design goals and constraints observed in the field
- Deterministic sequence: field teams must be able to run a linear sequence of idempotent steps. Avoid 'run these once and never again' operations.
- Minimized blast radius: make each step revertible; prefer operations that can be retried or rolled back without destructive state loss (e.g., keep control-plane node drainage before deleting vols).
- Support mixed inventory: same sequence must handle bare-metal servers (PXE/IPMI) and vSphere VMs (API-driven) with feature toggles.
- Network-first sanity: networking and DNS must be validated before kubelet bootstrap. Many failures observed are due to DNS/CNI misconfig or MTU mismatch.
- Telemetry hooks: each step should optionally emit a short JSON status object to the control-plane (or a local file) for operators and the Console to show progress.

High-level sequence (linear, idempotent steps)
1) Preflight inventory and health check (network, DNS, IPAM, NTP, image availability)
   - Validate access to registry/artifact storage from each host.
   - Validate external NTP from all nodes (>= 5 min skew => fail).
   - IP uniqueness check for the planned control-plane addresses.
2) Provisioning layer
   - Bare-metal: trigger PXE -> ignition flow or use image-based flashing; ensure BMC credentials reachable.
   - vSphere: create VM templates or clone from golden image, apply customization spec for IP/DNS.
   - After provisioning, run a host-level agent to verify packages and kernel settings (overlay, fs, hugepages if needed).
3) Network fabric and DNS
   - Create vLANs/port groups per plan or validate existing groups.
   - Deploy a small DNS responder in a high-availability config (2 nodes) for cluster-internal names during init.
   - Validate MTU and path MTU discovery (common culprit for CNI issues).
4) Control-plane bootstrap (one node at a time, validators enabled)
   - Start kube-apiserver + etcd on first node with local-e2e health probes. Record the initial etcd snapshot.
   - Add additional control-plane nodes and validate quorum. If adding a node fails, fallback to previous snapshot and remove failed node.
5) CNI + service networking
   - Deploy chosen CNI (Calico/Antrea/Cilium). Validate IP pool allocation and cross-node pod-to-pod connectivity with a small test job.
6) Worker join and readiness gating
   - Add workers gradually. For each worker, run kubelet join, taint/untaint logic to gate workload placement.
   - Run a set of workload smoke tests (DNS resolution, nodePort -> service reachability).
7) Observability + ops agents
   - Install log/metric forwarders after core cluster networking validated (avoid log storms during bootstrap).
8) Post-install validation and snapshot
   - Capture etcd snapshot, collect cluster-state bundle (kubeadm config, CNI manifest versions, kernel logs).

Key failure modes and handling notes
- Etcd split-brain after partial control-plane failure: always ensure a fresh snapshot before control-plane edits. Automate snapshot creation on step entry.
- IPAM mismatch when mixing DHCP and static assignments: canonicalize plan to a single authority for the cluster (recommended: static for control-plane, DHCP for workers OR explicit DHCP reservation list).
- vSphere customization errors (cloud-init user-data mismatch): module should validate guest OS cloud-init output through guest tools before joining.
- MTU mismatch causing cross-node pod traffic failure: include a mandatory MTU probe in network preflight.

Rollback primitives (safe defaults)
- Control-plane: automated etcd snapshot + restore path. Keep last 3 snapshots and rotate every successful control-plane change.
- Machine reprovision: for VMs, plan includes delete->reclone path. For bare-metal, include image-flash or re-PXE step.
- DNS rollback: point the internal resolver back to previous IPs and wait for TTLs if a resolver change fails.

Suggested Terraform module interface (thin, opinionated, human-friendly)
Notes: modules should be small and composable. Provide separate modules for compute lifecycle, network, and bootstrap orchestration glue. Keep the bootstrap module declarative and call out steps rather than hide imperative flows.

Module: onprem_compute (implements either baremetal or vsphere)\- variables: [string list] - compute_type: "baremetal" | "vsphere"\- variables: [string list] - hosts: list of host objects (flattened strings): e.g. ["node-01|10.0.1.10|control|bmc-url"]\- variables: [string] - image_ref: image id or template name\- variables: [string] - provisioning_mode: "pxe" | "flash" | "clone"\- outputs: [string list] - host_ids: ["node-01","node-02"]

Module: onprem_network\- variables: [string] - cluster_cidr\- variables: [string] - service_cidr\- variables: [string] - mtu_override (optional)\- variables: [string] - vlan_map (list of flattened "name:id")\- outputs: [string list] - network_endpoints (list of vrf/portgroup names)

Module: onprem_bootstrap\- variables: [string] - control_plane_hosts (list of host ids)
- variables: [string] - etcd_backup_location (s3|nfs|local)
- variables: [string] - cni_choice (calico|cilium|antrea)
- variables: [string] - bootstrap_sequence (string enum: "network-first"|"provision-first")
- variables: [string] - telemetry_endpoint (optional)
- outputs: [string list] - cluster_state_bundle_path

Interface examples (flattened var conventions)
- Use flat strings for host entries to avoid nested maps in most Terraform users' stacks: "name|ipv4|role|bmc". This makes it easier for the field UI to produce lines in CSV.

Safety flags and operator switches (module-level vars)
- dry_run = true | false (default true)\- step_lock = "none"|"preflight"|"control-plane" (if set, lock at the orchestration level to prevent concurrent operations)\- auto_snapshot = true | false

Testing checklists for preflight (quick run)
- Docker/puller: curl registry -> docker pull minimal image from each host (or VM)
- DNS: dig cluster.local resolver from each node
- MTU: iperf or ping with DF set to test 1500/9000 paths
- Storage: create LV or attach disk and perform fio write/read test (10s of MB)

Upgrade plan sketch (minor and major)
- Minor (patch/minor k8s): run control-plane component upgrades one node at a time with immediate health probe validation. Keep auto_snapshot true. Staged rollout: control-plane 1->n, then CNI upgrade, then workers.
- Major (k8s version bump or OS kernel): bring up a canary cluster of same inventory, run full smoke tests, compare metrics and e2e tests, run draining/rollback scripts on a small subset before rolling wide.

Field run notes / operator tips
- Always run preflight with --telemetry to capture ephemeral failures. We found several installs where BMC credentials were correct but BMC firmware blocked SSH-less reset; the telemetry log captured the firmware error string.
- Keep a physical console policy: for first-control-plane boots on bare-metal, prioritize a serial over IPMI because it surfaces kernel panics earlier.
- For vSphere installs, prefer thin-provision golden templates to speed reprovision and reduce datastore usage during iterative testing.

Open questions and next steps
- Decide canonical format for host linefields (CSV vs HCL map). Preference from field teams is CSV-like flattened entries.
- Define a minimal telemetry payload schema (timestamp, step, host, status, short error) and a central collector endpoint stub for Console to show live progress.
- Implement a small test harness that runs the sequence against a local lab rack and an internal vSphere cluster to validate the idempotency guarantees.

Appendix: quick sample host lines (for module input)
- "cp-01|10.0.1.10|control|ipmi://bmc.local/UID1"
- "worker-01|10.0.1.50|worker|"  (empty BMC field means VM-managed / cloud)

Appendix: minimal telemetry JSON (one-liner per step)
- {"ts":"2025-01-18T15:24:00Z","step":"provision-baremetal","host":"cp-01","status":"ok","note":"image flashed"}

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally prescriptive about step ordering; the goal is to reduce surprises during field installs. Please review the proposed module variable names and the flattened host convention.
- If we like the telemetry stub, I can draft a tiny collector service and a Console widget to visualize the sequence.

-- Jordan
